claims.statement: The dispatcher treats only validate and format as offline; other commands resolve credentials and connect before checking developer_mode, and force can override the non-developer gate only for upload and download, not destructive administration.
SesamNode construction can register a Portal analytics interaction before node connection or the developer-mode gate, so observational CLI entrypoints are not wholly side-effect-free.

Local operations are working-directory-sensitive: BASE_DIR records launch CWD, generic configuration lookup searches current and parent directories without changing process CWD, and connector detection/upload use connector_dir and handler chdir transitions.

Node/JWT resolution is delegated to sesamclient.utils.get_node_and_jwt_token using the CLI node, JWT and sync-config filename; locally implemented JSON/INI parsing does not establish that dependency's credential precedence.

The profile argument defaults to test and selects a relative <profile>-env.json file; upload merges ../.additional_parameters.json into that profile in memory with additional-parameter values overriding profile keys before environment replacement.

Whitelist handling is per handler rather than a global safety boundary: file/pipe filters apply in selected sync/test paths, while wipe performs node-wide configuration and environment replacement without whitelist filtering.

Connector expansion removes an existing expanded output directory and recreates generated config/profile files; validation dispatch expands first, so offline validation is not a local no-write inspection operation.

Connector validation rejects nonempty sink.dataset in list-form pipe templates and checks expanded JSON, WARNING descriptions, collect/share transform consistency, completeness references and share batch_size=1; its hardcoded .expanded walk and slash-suffix checks limit custom-path and OS portability.

Download overwrites the selected local environment profile and deletes selected local pipe/system files before formatting and extracting remote configuration; connector download can subsequently collapse the downloaded files into templates and manifest.

Status compares local and remote configuration/environment without raising merely for differences or a missing profile; missing connector expansion is also log-only, and status can replace a local sesam-config.zip while gathering its inputs.
Publisher output reads are not strictly read-only because get_published_data enables a disabled pump before making its publisher GET, including paths used by verification and expected-output update.

Captured CLI logs may expose credentials: normal node debug logging only partially masks JWT, constructor failure logs the full URL and JWT at ERROR, vvv can enable HTTP debugging, and OAuth can include client_secret in its logged authorization URL.

Upload is staged without local rollback: optional sink-dataset deletion precedes environment replacement, archive/config upload follows environment replacement, deployment waiting follows config upload, and testdata follows deployment; a later failure can leave earlier writes intact.

Upload modifies ZIP node metadata to disable user pipes by default unless enabled and to disable eager microservice loading unless requested; standalone run does not apply these upload-time metadata flags.

Concurrent testdata upload records successful and failed jobs and raises TestDataUploadException after futures complete, while single-thread upload aborts on its first raised failure; neither path undoes earlier successful receiver posts.
Testdata receiver posts have bounded per-file retries with exponential delay and jitter for retryable HTTP/request failures rather than transaction-wide retry or rollback.

Deployment waiting monitors only user pipes currently in Deploying, uses a 30-minute default timeout and five-second polling, and therefore does not itself verify that all pipe configurations are valid.

Run strictly stops a prior scheduler before starting the internal scheduler; async scheduling requires a token and polls status, treating failed/not-running responses or request exceptions as run failure.

Scheduler execution can request resetting pipes and deleting sink datasets by default; a local testdata directory makes the client send delete_input_datasets=False, while absence leaves the server-default input deletion behavior in place.
The internal scheduler uses POST routes for starting/stopping and separate GET routes for token-based runner status and optional since/token log inspection.

Test sequences upload, deployment waiting, repeated run and verify, but its failure handler and run's handler only log/rethrow; dispatch finally only logs elapsed time and does not stop an interrupted scheduler or compensate remote writes.

Verification loads expected/*.test.json and fails for missing nonignored expected files or referenced output pipes; no specs merely warns and returns, whereas output mismatches and unreferenced output pipes fail when specs are present.

Update is a baseline-writing operation that can delete specs for vanished nonignored output pipes, create expected files/specs, remove ignored output files and overwrite expected data with current node output.

Expansion annotates reused-template datatypes whose template basename differs from the datatype, and collapse deliberately skips those datatypes while rewriting master templates and manifest with best-effort parameter string substitution.

Although documentation describes .sesamconfig.json formatstyle customization, current CLI formatting paths do not load/consume sesamconfig_file and call format_json without a style argument; expected JSON uses a separate sorted json.dumps path with encoding/HTML-escape flags, bulk expected formatting skips test specs, and formatting writes files in place.

Connector upload completes config/testdata upload before authentication unless skipped; OAuth callback catches separate secret and environment failures and can continue later writes after an earlier failure, so authentication is not transactional deployment success reporting.

OAuth and API-key login write secrets to all returned systems, whereas Tripletex selects the placeholder system; these helpers can report partial failures via logs/callback responses rather than raising them to dispatch.

Stop calls SesamNode.stop_internal_scheduler, POSTs /pipes/stop-run-all-pipes with default terminate_timeout=30 and raises on HTTP failure without separately validating returned JSON; its default catch rethrows, and run/wipe require stop success before proceeding.

Wipe strictly stops the scheduler, force-uploads local/default node metadata disabling signalling, C++ extensions and user pipes, force-uploads empty config, clears environment and waits for user pipes to disappear; config and environment error handlers rethrow without reverting earlier stages.

Wipe help promises deletion of user datasets, but the local handler contains no explicit dataset-deletion call; its empty-config upload is delegated and its completion check verifies filtered pipe disappearance, not all dataset deletion.

The disappearance wait defaults to 30 minutes with five-second polling and excludes pipes of system/search/replica/aggregator-storage-node origins and IDs containing :singlenode; success means only that no pipes matching the user-pipe filter remain.

Reset and restart suppress failures only in their preliminary stop(throw_error=False), then call SesamNode.reset or restart with restart_timeout and rethrow subsequent failures; help describes reset as database deletion/restart and restart as resource recovery, but those node operations are delegated rather than local config/environment clearing.

SesamNode reset/restart read old status, call reset_node/restart_node, require exactly {"message": "OK"}, and poll for changed node_start_time with caught status-read failures, monotonic timeout and three-second sleeps; this criterion is not a subsequent pipe/test health verification.

Restart timeout defaults to 15 minutes and help advertises zero as a verification skip, but reset/restart enter polling unconditionally; zero can succeed only if the first status shows a changed start time or otherwise time out almost immediately, and timeout does not undo the issued node operation.

The development README prescribes incrementing sesam.py's version on a branch, passing PR tests and review, merging, then creating a described GitHub Release with a tag corresponding to the new version and expecting asset attachment by workflow.

The inspected sesam_version is 2.11.13 and the version branch prints it and exits before command validation; the release workflow forwards the release tag to packaging without a shown equality check against sesam_version.

Release assets are built on the release-published event, not every tag push or draft creation, with Python 3.10 across macos-latest, ubuntu-22.04 and windows-latest; jobs checkout, run Bash install/package scripts and upload to the event release with GITHUB_TOKEN, without a test.sh step or test-job dependency.

install.sh uses Bash fail-fast/tracing, installs unpinned PyInstaller and user-upgraded requirements, detects OS via uname and freezes sesam.py with --onefile; Linux/Darwin use the colon add-data separator and the Windows branch uses a semicolon to include connector_cli.
Bundling connector_cli resources supports connector generation's PackageLoader-based loading of shim.json, rather than packaging only the sesam.py script.

Packaging creates Linux and macOS tar.gz archives containing sesam and a Windows ZIP containing sesam.exe; the local macOS asset_path is dist/sesam-macos-TAG.tar.gz but the published asset_name is sesam-osx-TAG.tar.gz, while Linux/Windows names match their local archive basenames.
Package archive utilities are tar -zcf for Linux/macOS and 7z a for Windows, and release upload content types are application/tar for tarballs and application/zip for Windows ZIP.

install-latest.sh supports exact OSTYPE linux-gnu and darwin-prefix values, resolves the latest GitHub tag using curl, expects linux/osx tagged tarball asset names and extracts via wget/tar; it defaults to sesam-latest and moves into CWD for non-root or /usr/local/bin for root without verifying PATH/execution success.

install-tag.sh requires SESAM_TAG, supports only exact OSTYPE linux-gnu/darwin values and expects linux/osx tarball release names; it extracts in CWD and removes the archive without installing or renaming the executable onto PATH.

Operational helper portability depends on three different OS selectors—runner-label OS for package/test scripts, uname for freezing and OSTYPE for downloads—and on Bash/archive/download utilities and relative paths; package/download helpers lack fail-fast settings and download variables are unquoted, so their success messages and arbitrary-path handling are not robust verification.

OAuth login runs Flask on port 5010 and its shutdown helper shells out to lsof -i tcp:5010, parses the PID column and SIGKILLs every returned PID rather than tracking only its own server; the release Windows asset does not establish portability or safe port ownership for this strategy.

Historical installation documentation describes PATH-deployed binaries and Python 3.5+ Linux/OSX source/PyInstaller examples, whereas workflows specify Python 3.10 and requirements constrain dependencies; these sources do not establish current compatibility or successful installation/build/download results.

The source-established distribution path is the sesam.py main entrypoint or its one-file executable archives, not a wheel or installed console entry point; pyproject.toml and setup.cfg shown here are formatter/linter configurations rather than distribution metadata.

PR tests are path-filtered to Python files, requirements.txt and test.yml and use Python 3.10 on the three release OS labels; max-parallel=1 and sesam_py_environment concurrency protect their shared remote CI node, and jobs build then run test.sh with a secret-provided token.

test.sh selects dist/sesam or dist/sesam.exe by runner OS, invokes help, supplies a fixed remote CI target/token environment and executes run_test.sh inside each non-symlink test directory, making it remote integration testing rather than safe local triage.

The fair-weather integration script retries commands up to three times, resets before/after, exercises whitelist upload/run/verify with pytest, update, status and download, and asserts retained ZIP existence; its pytest check enforces no underscores in local pipe filenames/IDs, not status drift failure or formatstyle-option consumption.

The embedded conversion integration script retries commands, copies input configuration to a working tree, wipes, converts, tests with extracted testdata, resets and recursively compares expected_after, so it is destructive remote integration coverage rather than a production recovery procedure.

The inspected integration scripts do not assert partial-write rollback, scheduler interruption cleanup, best-effort stop suppression, zero-timeout verification skip, OAuth partial-failure behavior or release-download correctness; the documented limits for those cases come from implementation inspection rather than claimed test passes.
